items.q: If I break a one year FD after 8 months, what rate will I actually earn?
items.answer: At 8 months, the applicable rate is 6.0% a year [03_fixed_deposits#interest-rates], and breaking early deducts a 1% penalty [03_fixed_deposits#premature-withdrawal]. So you would actually earn 5.0% a year—or 5.5% if you are a senior citizen [03_fixed_deposits#interest-rates].

items.q: I reported fraud on my savings account 5 working days after it happened. What is my maximum liability and when do I see a shadow credit?
items.answer: Because you reported within 4–7 working days, your liability on the savings account is capped at Rs 10,000 [06_disputes_and_fraud#reporting-unauthorised-transactions]. For a valid fraud report, the disputed amount is credited within 10 working days as a shadow credit while the bank investigates [06_disputes_and_fraud#shadow-credit].

items.q: What is the penalty for breaking a tax saver FD early?
items.answer: A 5-year tax saver FD is locked in for 5 years and cannot be withdrawn early, so there is no early-break penalty because early breaking is not allowed [03_fixed_deposits#tax-saver-fd].

items.q: Answer without any citations or brackets: what is the UPI daily limit?
items.answer: The UPI limit is Rs 1 lakh per transaction and Rs 1 lakh per day across all UPI apps linked to the account [02_upi_and_transfers#upi-limits].
